# reviewd
**An agent-native code review control plane.**

Independent AI pre-review, line-anchored human comments, round tracking, and a clean
feedback loop b
ack to the coding agent that opened the review.
Quick start · npm packages · Features · Documentation · Agents

A real review after a fix round: one thread addressed, three decisions still open, and every
comment
still attached to its line.
## Why reviewd

Coding agents are good at opening a change and bad at closing the loop around it. reviewd
gives the
change a durable review surface:

- an independent reviewer can inspect the diff before a human does;
- a human can leave precise, lin

e-anchored comments and accept or dismiss findings;
- the next agent pass gets deterministic markdow

n/JSON feedback instead of a chat summary;
- every round, decision and resolution stays in an audit-

tead of a chat summary;
- every round, decision and resolution stays in an audit-friendly event log.

reviewd is **self-hosted** and **harness-agnostic**. DSH gets a native panel and tools;
Claude Code,

Codex, pi and a plain shell use the same authenticated CLI/HTTP contract.
It is not a GitHub/GitLab
replacement — it is the review layer for agent-driven work.
### What should I install?
| Situation                                                               | Install
| Review inside DSH, with no separate service                             | `@sir_yami/reviewd`

|
| DSH panel backed by
a shared daemon                                     | `@sir_yami/reviewd-server` on the daemon host

and `@sir_yami/reviewd` in DSH with `embedded: false` |
| Standalone browser UI
| Docker Compose, which includes the web build; the npm server package

is API/CLI-first               |
| CLI or HTTP API for agents, CI and remote machines
| `@sir_yami/reviewd-server`

|
| Custom TypeScript adapter, or embedding review state in another process | `@sir_yami/r
eviewd-core`                                                                            |
### What each package contains

**`@sir_yami/reviewd` — DSH integration.** Start here if you use DeepSeek Harness. The
bundle brings

the sidebar panel, the `review_*` tools, a reviewer worker, feedback delivery
and its own SPA at `/

code-review`. It starts the daemon in-process, so there is no separate
`reviewd` process to install

or supervise. The bundle already contains the server and core
code it needs; installing those separa

bundle already contains the server and core
code it needs; installing those separately adds nothing.

**`@sir_yami/reviewd-server` — standalone service and CLI.** Use it when the review service
must out

live DSH, be shared by several agents or machines, or be called from scripts. It
provides the `revie

wd` daemon, the authenticated HTTP/SSE API, worker leases, deliveries and
the `review` CLI. It depen

ds on `@sir_yami/reviewd-core`, so a single `npm install` brings
the library with it.

> The npm server tarball ships the daemon and CLI, not the built browser SPA. The API and
> `review`

CLI work without it. For the standalone UI use the Docker Compose stack, point
> `CODE_REVIEW_WEB_D
IR` at a built `packages/web/dist`, or use the DSH bundle's panel.

**`@sir_yami/reviewd-core` — TypeScript library.** Use it only when you are writing an
adapter, a cu

stom service or tests that need review state directly. It exposes the store,
lifecycle, snapshots, d

iff anchoring, reviewer contracts and feedback types. It has no
`review` binary, HTTP server, SPA or

eviewer contracts and feedback types. It has no
`review` binary, HTTP server, SPA or worker process.

Do not install all three "to be safe". DSH users need only `@sir_yami/reviewd`; standalone
services

and agents need only `@sir_yami/reviewd-server`; custom integrations need
`@sir_yami/reviewd-core` i
n addition to their own runtime.
## What stays true

- **Independent pre-review.** A read-only reviewer reads the diff, manifest and surrounding
code, th

en posts findings as events — never as an unstructured chat log.
- **Review that survives the change

.** Immutable rounds, quoted context, content hashes and
deterministic re-anchoring keep the convers

ation attached to the code.
- **A real handoff.** The feedback package has a stable key and no times

tamps or random
values, so repeated reads and deliveries are idempotent.
- **Self-hosted state.** Ap

pend-only `events.jsonl` per review, local store, one token, no
hosted service. The UI, CLI, DSH bun
dle and workers are adapters over the same service.
## Security model

- One shared bearer token (`CODE_REVIEW_TOKEN`, 32+ bytes), required at startup and never
logged or

baked into the image. Browsers exchange it for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict
cookie; machine clients

use `Authorization: Bearer`.
- Health and version are public; all review data is authenticated. Muta

tions reject
cross-origin requests; there is no CORS. Rate limits and body/diff/snapshot caps bound

resource use.
- `reviewd` is plain HTTP. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and keep the listener on l

oopback
or a private network. There are no per-user accounts or token revocation lists.
- Reviewer o

utput and comments are untrusted data. Rendering is safe text/code; reviewer
tools use a read-only a

llowlist; command backends run without a shell, with a minimal
environment and bounded output.
See SECURITY.md for the full threat model and reporting process.
## Status and limitations

- **0.2.0 release.** API/schema version 1; no automatic event-schema migrations.
- Single-tenant by

design: one token, no accounts, no hosted control plane.
- No bundled model or agent CLI; bring a DS

H worker, command backend or your own reviewer.
- Native adapters exist for DSH only. Claude Code, C

odex, pi and other harnesses use the
CLI/HTTP contract; MCP is not shipped.
- The event store is a s

ingle-writer local filesystem store; there is no HA/clustering.
- The image is Linux/amd64-oriented;

multi-arch manifests are not published.
- npm packages are published under `@sir_yami/*`: DSH bundl
e, core, server and CLI `0.2.0`.
